hypothesis_loop.hypothesis: After a covered flood loss, insurer-funded resilience money creates a temporary high-intent retrofit market. Because the customer is already rebuilding, specification, accredited-product selection and contractor coordination should matter more than pre-event consumer advertising.

exact_analysis_questions.how_much_more_for_convenience_certainty_: The end customer's effective BBB budget can be up to £10k because the insurer funds it after a claim. Recent average home flood claims are roughly £60k–£90k, making the maximum resilience budget ~11–17% of average claim cost. This is payer-funded budget, not consumer WTP.
exact_analysis_questions.which_problem_states_show_strongest_econ: Freshly flooded insured home during reinstatement—especially repeat-flood or high-reconstruction-cost properties—where walls/floors/electrics are already being rebuilt and incremental resilience is easier to install.
exact_analysis_questions.current_options: Insurer/loss-adjuster BBB workflow, PFR surveyors, EA-framework suppliers, flood-door/barrier/pump/non-return-valve manufacturers, resilient-building contractors, loss assessors.
exact_analysis_questions.is_there_room_for_us: Potentially yes in conversion/delivery rather than product discovery: BBB eligibility explanation, early PFR survey, certified solution specification, supplier availability, insurer-compliant evidence/FPC data. Direct consumer acquisition is constrained because the insurer/loss adjuster owns the claim event.
exact_analysis_questions.best_gtm: Partner with insurers, loss adjusters, brokers, local authorities or flood-recovery firms. Trigger at FNOL/claim acceptance rather than generic SEO. Build a standardized PFR survey/specification + certified supplier availability + evidence record.
exact_analysis_questions.same_pattern_other_country: B11 Direct Line funded up to £500 leak detection after a >£7.5k water loss. B12 independently shows up to £10k flood-resilience budget after insured flood loss. The post-loss prevention-budget mechanism replicates strongly.
exact_analysis_questions.why_country_difference: UK Flood Re creates a formal industry-wide resilience framework because flood insurance affordability is a public-policy/insurance-system issue. The payer and claim workflow are highly institutionalized.
exact_analysis_questions.what_does_it_reveal_about_country: The UK is building a standardized property-resilience information infrastructure around insurance, certified products, trained claims professionals and future Flood Performance Certificates.
exact_analysis_questions.macro_pattern: A loss event can create both budget and temporary installation efficiency: damaged finishes are already open/replacing, so resilience measures can piggyback on reinstatement. But the claim gatekeeper controls whether the customer ever sees the opportunity.
exact_analysis_questions.falsifier_result: Funding is large enough and market coverage broad, so hypothesis supported. However, low take-up and small/certification-constrained supply mean the issue is not lack of nominal funding. It is conversion, trusted specification, procurement and claim-workflow ownership.

mechanism_candidates.statement: When resilience funding is unlocked inside an insurance claim, the claims handler/loss adjuster becomes the primary distribution gatekeeper; nominal customer eligibility does not translate automatically into demand.
mechanism_candidates.observed_context: Take-up remains around one third of those offered despite broad insurer participation; FloodReady prioritizes claim-point communication and professional training.
mechanism_candidates.next_replication_test: Test another claim-funded repair/upgrade market where adjusters or approved repair networks mediate customer choice.

mechanism_candidates.statement: A specialist mitigation market whose residential demand is primarily triggered by disasters/grants experiences volatile demand and weak standing capacity, creating post-event procurement bottlenecks.
mechanism_candidates.observed_context: 2023 study: small supplier base, post-event demand, installers can add 20–40% in 2–4 months and manufacturers ~20%, with limited willingness to scale absent guaranteed demand.
mechanism_candidates.next_replication_test: Test storm-roofing, wildfire remediation or disaster restoration markets with event-linked contractor capacity.

mechanism_candidates.statement: As standardized proof of property resilience becomes portable across insurance, lending and housing transactions, the evidence record itself can become economically valuable.
mechanism_candidates.next_replication_test: Observe whether 2026-27 Flood Performance Certificate pilots actually influence premiums, lending, saleability or insurer workflows.

next_probe.sector: insurance-funded residential roof repair/replacement after hail/wind
next_probe.selection_reason: B12 generated EVENT_GATED_SUPPLY_MARKET and CLAIM_GATEKEEPER_CONTROLS_FUNDED_DEMAND. US hail/storm roofing is a structurally different, highly mature post-loss market with insurer adjusters, contractor surges, code/roof compatibility, fraud/scam risk and large weather-driven demand pulses. It is an excellent negative/replication control for whether event-funded markets inevitably create middleman whitespace.
next_probe.hypothesis: Post-event insurer-funded replacement creates strong demand but may become so contractor-saturated and claims-optimized that independent intermediary whitespace disappears; the useful value may shift to trusted contractor verification, scope/estimate normalization and fraud-resistant evidence.
falsifiers: Storm roofing is not materially insurer-funded.
Contractor supply does not surge after hail events.
Adjuster/claim workflows do not control replacement economics.
The market remains fragmented enough that neutral routing has strong whitespace despite maturity.
